Crochet Spider Coasters Tutorial

Small black spiders with big googly eyes that double as coasters — spooky, cute, and a quick gift for coffee lovers.

Hi friend, it's Sara here. I designed these to be truly beginner friendly — the coaster base is a flat circle and the spider body is a tiny ball, then we add eight little chain legs. No complicated sewing, just one hour per spider.

Level Beginner — magic ring, single crochet, chains for legs
Yarn Worsted — about 14 yds black per spider + 2 yds white for eyes — 4mm hook — 8mm safety eyes — polyfill — set of 4 about 56 yds black
Size Coaster about 4.6" across × spider body about 2" wide — gauge 20 sc x 24 rows = 4" — about 1 hour per coaster

Before you begin

I love these spiders because they are not scary at all. They sit on your mug and look up at you with those big eyes. The coaster part protects the table, and the spider part makes people smile.

We will make a flat black circle for the coaster, about 4.6" across. Then we make a small black ball for the spider body, add eight chain legs, stuff lightly, and sew it to the center of the coaster. The eyes are big white circles with black safety eyes in the middle — that is what makes them cute instead of spooky.

We work in continuous rounds with a marker. Keep your tension relaxed with black yarn — it can be hard to see, so work near a window.

Materials

  • Worsted weight yarn (medium 4) in Black — about 14 yards per spider coaster (about 10 yds for flat base + 4 yds for body + legs) — about 56 yards for set of 4
  • Worsted in White — about 2 yards per coaster for eye patches
  • 4mm (G-6) crochet hook
  • 8mm black safety eyes — 2 per spider — safety note: safety eyes are a choking hazard for children under 3; embroider eyes with black yarn instead for babies and party favors for small children
  • Polyester fiberfill — small pinch per spider, about 2 oz for 4
  • Yarn needle, scissors, stitch marker

Yarn estimate from stitch count: flat coaster base R1-R12 = 390 sts total, spider body R1-R17 = about 318 sts total, 8 legs × (10 ch + 9 sc) = about 152 sts, white eyes 2 × 18 sts = 36 sts — about 896 sts total per coaster — at 20 sc = 4" (about 0.2" per st) about 8-10 yards black + 1-2 yards white + small amounts for sewing — I suggest about 14 yards black per coaster to be safe (about 56 yards for set of 4) — measure your own finished coaster for your most accurate number.

Sizing & gauge

Gauge: 20 sc x 24 rows = 4" x 4" in single crochet with 4mm hook and worsted yarn. Each stitch about 0.2" wide.

Math for this coaster:
Coaster base diameter = sts × 0.2" ÷ 3.14
R6 (36 sts): 36 × 0.2 ÷ 3.14 = about 2.29"
R9 (54 sts): 54 × 0.2 ÷ 3.14 = about 3.44"
R12 (72 sts): 72 × 0.2 ÷ 3.14 = about 4.58" — main coaster size, about 4.6" across — perfect for mug
Spider body: R4 (24 sts): 24 × 0.2 ÷ 3.14 = about 1.53" diameter flat → about 1.8" wide stuffed, about 2" long with head + body

Abbreviations

MR — magic ring: loop yarn, pull up loop, ch 1, work stitches into loop, pull tail to close. No hole.
ch — chain
sl st — slip stitch
sc — single crochet
inc — increase: 2 sc in same stitch
inv dec — invisible decrease: front loops of next 2 sts, yarn over pull through 2, yarn over pull through 2 — closes without bump, used only for spider body
FO — fasten off
[...] x6 — repeat 6 times

Roadmap — 6 steps

1. Flat black circle for coaster base
2. Small black ball for spider body
3. Eight chain legs
4. Big googly eyes
5. Stuff body
6. Sew spider to center of coaster

Step 1: Flat coaster base

This is just a flat circle. We increase by 6 each round to stay flat. If it starts to bowl, add a little more slack. If it waves, you have too many increases — count to 72 at the end.

With Black — Coaster Base:
R1: MR, 6 sc into ring (6)
R2: inc x6 (12)
R3: (sc 1, inc) x6 (18)
R4: (sc 2, inc) x6 (24)
R5: (sc 3, inc) x6 (30)
R6: (sc 4, inc) x6 (36) — about 2.29"
R7: (sc 5, inc) x6 (42) — about 2.67"
R8: (sc 6, inc) x6 (48) — about 3.05"
R9: (sc 7, inc) x6 (54) — about 3.44"
R10: (sc 8, inc) x6 (60) — about 3.82"
R11: (sc 9, inc) x6 (66) — about 4.20"
R12: (sc 10, inc) x6 (72) — about 4.58" — main coaster size
Sl st to first st, FO leaving 10" tail for weaving — no stuffing

Flat black circle, 72 stitches, about 4.6" across at R12, coaster base.

What it should look like now: Flat black disc about 4.6" across, 72 sts around, lies flat on table.

Step 2: Spider body — little ball

Now the spider itself. Two small balls — one slightly bigger for abdomen, one smaller for head — or one ball with two sections. I make it as one piece: bottom big, top smaller.

With Black — Spider Body (worked as one piece, bottom to top):
R1: MR, 6 sc (6)
R2: inc x6 (12)
R3: (sc 1, inc) x6 (18)
R4: (sc 2, inc) x6 (24) — about 1.53" diameter flat
R5-R8: sc around (24) — 4 rounds even — about 0.66" tall
R9: (sc 2, inv dec) x6 (18) — start closing abdomen
R10: (sc 1, inv dec) x6 (12) — stuff lightly here
R11: inc x12 (24) — double every stitch to start head — (24)
R12-R14: sc around (24) — 3 rounds for head
R15: (sc 2, inv dec) x6 (18)
R16: (sc 1, inv dec) x6 (12)
R17: inv dec x6 (6) — close, FO leaving 12" tail

Small black dome, first part of spider body, about 1.5" across before stuffing.

What it should look like now: Small figure-8 shape with bigger bottom and smaller top, about 2" long total, open at top before final close.

Step 3: Eight legs with chains

The legs are just chains that curl a little on their own. Make them all the same length — I use a piece of cardboard to measure.

With Black — 8 Legs (make 8):
Ch 10, sc in 2nd ch from hook and in each ch across (9) — about 2" leg — FO leaving 6" tail
Make 8 legs — 4 per side

Small black spider with eight chain legs attached, four per side, each about 2" long.

What it should look like now: Spider body with 8 legs sewn evenly around middle, 4 on each side, legs about 2" long, slight curl.

Step 4: Big googly eyes

The eyes are what make them cute. I crochet small white circles first, then add safety eyes in the middle.

With White — Eye Patches (make 2):
R1: MR, 6 sc (6)
R2: inc x6 (12) — about 0.76" across
FO leaving 8" tail
Place 8mm safety eye through center of white patch, then place patches on head between R12-R13, about 4 sts apart — about 0.8" apart (4 × 0.2") — sew white patches to head
Or embroider black pupils with black yarn if not using safety eyes — required for children under 3

Placing large white eye patches with black safety eyes on black spider head, about 0.8" apart.

What it should look like now: Spider with two big white eyes with black centers, about 4 sts apart on head.

Step 5: Stuffing and closing

Stuff just the body lightly — not the coaster base. The coaster stays flat.

Stuffing:
Stuff abdomen and head lightly — small pinch each — about grape size total
Close top with inv dec x6, weave tail inside

Hands crocheting and attaching legs to small black spider, chain legs about 2" long.

What it should look like now: Plump little spider about 2" long × 1.8" wide, lightly stuffed, 8 legs attached, big eyes on.

Step 6: Attach spider to coaster

Now we put it together. Sew the spider to the center of the flat coaster base with black yarn. Go through the bottom of spider and through coaster base several times.

Assembly:
Place spider body in center of coaster base (R12 72 sts coaster)
With black tail, sew through bottom of spider and through coaster base — 4-5 stitches — secure tightly
FO and weave all tails under coaster base
Finished coaster about 4.6" across with 2" spider on top

Finished small black crochet spider with big white eyes and eight legs, sitting on coaster base, about 4.6" coaster with 2" spider.

What it should look like now: Finished spider coaster — flat black coaster about 4.6" across with small 3D spider sewn in center, 8 legs splayed, cute googly eyes.

Assembly and finishing

  1. Make flat coaster base R1-R12 = 72 sts = about 4.6" across — no stuffing.
  2. Make spider body R1-R17 as figure-8 shape, stuff lightly between R10 and R15.
  3. Make 8 legs ch 10, sc 9 — sew 4 per side around middle of body at R9-R11.
  4. Make 2 white eye patches R1-R2 = 12 sts = about 0.76" across, insert safety eyes, sew to head 4 sts apart (0.8" apart).
  5. Sew spider to center of coaster base.
  6. Weave all tails under coaster base, trim.

Troubleshooting

Coaster bowls or waves: Bowls = too few inc — need 6 inc per round to 72. Waves = too many inc — count: R12 should be 72, not 60 or 84.

Black yarn hard to see: Work near bright window or clip small light to project — count stitches by feel with marker every 12 sts.

Spider body too pointy: Missed increases — R4 should be 24 before straight section.

Legs different lengths: Ch 10 exactly for each — use same tension — count 9 sc per leg.

Eyes too far apart: Place 4 sts apart = 0.8" at this gauge — pin first to test.

Coaster not flat after sewing spider: Sew only through top loops of coaster base, not pulling tight — keep coaster flat.

Ways to make it your own

Size changes at 20 sc = 4" gauge — each st 0.2" wide — diameter = sts × 0.2 ÷ 3.14:
- Small 3.8" coaster: R1 6, R2 12, R3 18, R4 24, R5 30, R6 36, R7 42, R8 48, R9 54, R10 60 — about 3.82" across — use for espresso cups — about 8 yds black
- Main 4.6" coaster: R1 6, R2 12, R3 18, R4 24, R5 30, R6 36, R7 42, R8 48, R9 54, R10 60, R11 66, R12 72 — about 4.58" across — this pattern — about 10 yds black for base
- Large 5.7" coaster: R1 6, R2 12, R3 18, R4 24, R5 30, R6 36, R7 42, R8 48, R9 54, R10 60, R11 66, R12 72, R13 78 (sc 12, inc) x6, R14 84 (sc 13, inc) x6, R15 90 (sc 14, inc) x6 — about 5.73" across — about 14 yds
- Spider size: Tiny 1.5" spider — R1 6, R2 12, R3 18, R4 18 sc around 3 rounds, R5 (sc 1, dec) x6 (12), R6 dec x6 (6) — about 1.5" — ch 8 for legs (7 sc)
- Color: make purple spiders with green eyes for fun Halloween
- No safety eyes: embroider eyes with white and black yarn — required for children under 3
— Sara

Thank you for making these spooky little spider coasters with me. I hope they make your coffee table a little cuter and your Halloween a little cozier. Quick pattern — corrected

  • 4mm hook — black about 14 yds per spider coaster
  • Coaster base: 6→12→18→24→30→36→42→48→54→60→66→72 = 4.58" — main size
  • Spider body: 6→12→18→24, 4 rounds even, dec to 18→12, inc to 24 for head, 3 rounds even, dec 18→12→6
  • Legs: ch 10, sc 9 × 8 legs, 4 per side
  • Eyes: white patch 12 sts + 8mm safety eye — 4 sts apart = 0.8"
  • Safety: embroider eyes for under 3
